item.title: Hamilton & Verstappen to start from back in Brazil
item.description: Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will both start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix [Reuters] Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also have grid penalties, 10 places for Leclerc and five for Russell. Hamilton initially had only a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season, but the new internal combustion engine that was fitted on Saturday morning failed in final practice. That meant Ferrari decided to fit an entire new power-unit to his car, hence the bigger penalty. Verstappen had an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc and Russell have both fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalty for Leclerc is bigger than Russell's because it is the first time Ferrari have exceeded the limit of four engines per season on his car, while Russell had already gone beyond that. The four drivers are separated by just 16 points in the drivers' championship, in the battle to finish second behind Kimi Antonelli. Verstappen famously won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Qualifying is set to be wet, after rain started about an hour before the session, and it is expected to continue overnight, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." item.title: Arsenal 1-0 Hull analysis: Win means penalty drama can be overlooked
item.description: Arsenal have a 100% record at home in the Premier League this season [Getty Images] Arsenal showed their champion mentality on Saturday to keep coming at Hull despite initially struggling to create chances. Things could have felt very different if Martin Odegaard had not have swept home his winner though. Mikel Arteta's team had had a penalty shout turned down in the first period after Kai Havertz's shirt was pulled in the box by Nobel Mendy. The decision was not given on the field although the Video Assistant Referee told referee Farai Hallam to look at the pitchside monitor. Hallam then informed the crowd Havertz had been fouled, but no penalty would be awarded as the forward had been in an offside position. Similar to an incident in their win over Liverpool last week in which Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt but the Reds were denied a penalty, the decision may have been headline news if Odegaard had not gone on to net the winner. Instead Arsenal celebrated their ninth win in 11 matches and extended their unbeaten home run in all competitions to 11 games.

item.title: Giants See Milton As Key To Ending 13-year Linc Drought
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The New York Giants enter Sunday with a clear goal: snap a 13-year winless streak at Lincoln Financial Field, according to Big Blue View . This mission gets harder because the Eagles swapped quarterbacks just days before the game. Joe Milton replaces Tanner McKee, bringing a physical style that changes how the Giants must prepare. Giants head coach John Harbaugh knows the shift is coming. He admitted he heard the news before practice on Wednesday. “Word travels fast,” Harbaugh said jokingly. “We’ve seen Joe in college,” he said. A New Threat in the Pocket Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson expects Milton to bring a different dynamic to the offense. Milton stands 6-foot-5 and weighs 246 pounds, offering size and mobility that McKee lacks. Wilson told reporters that Milton can run and is elusive in the pocket. “He can throw the ball 100 yards,” Wilson said. “So we have to be aware of that. He’s going to bring a different dynamic to the offense, and we’re really aware of it.” The Giants cannot just prepare for the standard Eagles scheme. They must anticipate how Milton uses his legs to extend plays and create new angles. Forget the Past, Play the Game Harbaugh joked about inheriting a bad debt from a dead relative when asked about the long losing streak in Philly. “You got all the pictures and the record collection and you got the million dollar debt that your uncle incurred,” Harbaugh said jokingly. “I’d say, ‘I’m not up for that so I’m gonna say no thanks to that.'” The team refuses to let history dictate the game plan. Tight end Isaiah Likely echoed this mindset, noting he wasn’t there for the losses a decade ago. “Whether whatever record was in the past. I mean, I wasn’t here 13 years ago, so my mentality is winning the game at hand,” Likely said. The focus remains on finishing 1-0 every single week. Giants Ready for Sunday Showdown The Giants come into this matchup well-rested after a bye week. They hold a 4-2-1 record and lead the NFC East. The Eagles, meanwhile, are on a six-game losing streak and rank last in yards per play. Despite the Eagles’ struggles, the Giants know they cannot get lazy. They must match the intensity of a team desperate for a spark. Harbaugh noted that while Milton changes things, it is still the Eagles’ offense and structure. The game takes place on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m.

item.title: Hawks’ Newell, Gilbert Sidelined As Frontcourt Depth Shrinks
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Atlanta Hawks frontcourt just got thinner. The team confirmed on Friday that two young players will miss significant time with injuries. Second-year big man Asa Newell hyperextended his left big toe during Wednesday’s win in Washington. He faces a reevaluation in about two weeks, but that does not guarantee a return. On Thursday, guard Keshon Gilbert had a non-surgical procedure done to treat left knee inflammation, the Hawks stated. Per the team, Gilbert is scheduled for reevaluation in roughly six weeks. This timing hurts a roster already dealing with losses. Jalen Johnson and Jock Landale are out for their third straight game. Johnson suffered a left ankle sprain while Landale deals with a left hip strain. The team is also missing Mouhamed Gueye and Henri Veesaar, who are recovering from long-term injuries. With Newell and Gilbert gone, the rotation gets tight fast. Seven games are on the Hawks’ schedule for the upcoming two weeks, featuring a November 20 home matchup versus Charlotte. That could be Newell’s reevaluation date. Depth Test for Young Roster Atlanta drafted Newell 23rd overall in the 2025 draft. He has shown promise in his limited minutes this season. Across five games, the 20-year-old posted 2.6 rebounds and 3.6 points while playing 11.0 minutes per contest. Atlanta exercised the option for his third year on Sunday, indicating the club intends to keep him. Now he faces a setback just as he started to earn rotation minutes. The team says another update “will be provided at that time” regarding his status. According to reports, the recovery timeline likely extends past the two-week threshold. Gilbert brings a different skill set as a former UNLV and Iowa State standout. He plays on a two-way contract, which gives the Hawks flexibility but also limits his availability. The procedure on his left knee was non-surgical, which is good news for a quick fix, but six weeks is still a long stretch for a two-way player. The injuries have required the coaching staff to rely on veterans and promote additional practice‑squad players. AJC.com reported that the team’s frontcourt depth will be tested early in the season. Rotation Shifts and Roles The loss of Newell and Gilbert changes how the team handles its big men. Although initially questionable for Friday’s Wizards rematch, Jalen Johnson has been downgraded to out. He missed his third straight game. Landale’s absence on Friday represents the third consecutive time he has missed a game. The Hawks have already seen Kingston Flemings get more opportunities as time passed. Flemings played a career-high 28 minutes against the Miami Heat and scored 23 points. CJ McCollum, the veteran, suggested the lineup change himself and has now yielded the starting role. McCollum is playing out of position and averaging a career-low 26.8 minutes per game. While he can still score, he lacks the skill set of a lead guard without Trae Young on the floor. item.title: Arsenal 1-0 Hull City: Ødegaard Strikes As Gunners Go Six Points Clear
item.description: Arsenal 1-0 Hull City: Ødegaard Strikes As Gunners Go Six Points Clear Arsenal were made to work incredibly hard for their three points at the Emirates Stadium this afternoon, with Martin Ødegaard’s 72nd-minute winner finally breaking down a stubborn Hull City side. It certainly wasn’t a vintage Arsenal performance, but another victory and another clean sheet see Mikel Arteta’s Gunners extend their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points, ahead of Manchester City’s later fixture. Hull Frustrate Arsenal As VAR Takes Centre Stage Arsenal started brightly, with Gabriel coming agonisingly close to getting on the end of an Ezri Konsa shot inside the opening six minutes, but Hull were certainly not there simply to make up the numbers. David Raya was forced into a good save from Elliot Stroud, while Christos Tzolis looked lively for Arsenal, although a promising break ended with Kai Havertz caught offside. Declan Rice saw a volley go narrowly wide before having a dangerous free kick saved, while Tzolis also threatened with a header. The biggest talking point of the first half came when Havertz appeared to be pulled down inside the penalty area by Nobel Mendy. Following an on-field VAR review, however, the referee ruled Havertz offside and no penalty was awarded, with the Emirates crowd making their frustration very clear! Arsenal went into half-time goalless, with Hull having done an excellent job of frustrating the champions. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Ødegaard Finally Makes The Breakthrough The second half followed a similar pattern, with Arsenal pushing forward but struggling to find that elusive opening goal. Madueke was particularly dangerous, forcing saves from Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, while Arteta introduced Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino for Havertz and Rice in the 63rd minute. Eberechi Eze and Piero Hincapié followed shortly afterwards as Arsenal searched for a breakthrough. Finally, in the 72nd minute, the pressure paid off. Madueke cut inside and fired a low effort towards goal. Tzolakis could only parry the ball into the path of Ødegaard, who reacted quickest to put Arsenal ahead. Relief around the Emirates! Arsenal continued looking for a second, with Merino and Gyökeres both testing the Hull goalkeeper, but the visitors refused to surrender and pushed for an equaliser in the closing stages. There was even another penalty appeal in stoppage time when Madueke went down inside the area, but nothing was given. It wasn’t pretty, and Hull certainly made life difficult for Arsenal, although their physical approach frequently crossed the line. Five yellow cards for the visitors, compared to none for Arsenal, tell their own story, with Tzolis on the receiving end of some particularly nasty challenges. Nevertheless, the Gunners kept their composure and once again demonstrated their ability to grind out a result. Three more points, another clean sheet and a six-point lead at the top of the table. item.title: Joshua Kimmich believes ‘calm’ Bayern Munich could be building something very special
item.description: MAINZ, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 07: Joshua Kimmich of FC Bayern Muenchen celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between 1. FSV Mainz 05 and FC Bayern München at MEWA Arena on November 07, 2026 in Mainz, Germany. (Photo by A. Scheuber/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images There is a reason Bayern Munich has earned the nickname FC Hollywood . From presidents who end up in jail to players burning down their houses, constant public sniping, regular infighting, and frequent coaching changes, unrest and tension amid success have long been the norm for Die Rekordmeister . In some ways, that instability has been the bedrock of the Bavarians’ success, as the club has never grown comfortable enough to rest on its laurels or lower its very high standards. However, stability is also vital in building a club to greater heights. Drama remains at the core and will never truly go away as long as the club maintains its high standards, but the last few years have seen the club enter a state of relative calm not experienced in a long time. Unsurprisingly, these years coincide with the appointment of Vincent Kompany, whose calm and collected manner has helped ease tensions at the club. Bayern’s vice-captain, Joshua Kimmich, believes that this calm has been crucial in the team’s recent development. “I’ve experienced different things during my 11 years here,” the 31-year-old said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) after Bayern’s 2-1 away win over Mainz in the Bundesliga. “What’s come together over the last two or three years is really special—with the coach, the coaching staff, the team, and everyone around the club. There’s a lot of calm at the club at the moment. Things used to be different. Even when we were playing successful football, there was still a lot of unrest. Now, you really get the feeling that everything is falling into place. Of course, we have to be successful on the pitch—that’s always the foundation. But we’ve seen over the past few weeks that even when the coach is unavailable and we have a lot of injuries, we still stand together. And I think that’s also what matters in football.” This bedrock for the Bavarians’ success is what is keeping their season going despite all the setbacks. It is quite admirable. item.title: Westwood Warns DP World Tour Faces Hard Truths As LIV Collapses
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Lee Westwood sees a rough road ahead for the DP World Tour now that LIV Golf has stopped operations. The former world number one believes the European circuit lost its main bargaining chip the moment the breakaway tour shut its doors. Westwood told BBC Sport on Friday that the end of LIV might not be the victory everyone expects for Europe. He suggests the PGA Tour should stop handing out money without demanding much in return. The Leverage Is Gone For years, LIV players could not touch PGA Tour events but could still play on the DP World Tour. This rule gave the European circuit a unique advantage in talks with the Americans. Westwood noted that this setup gave them some “leverage” while the rival tour was still active. The 53-year-old explained the situation clearly in his interview with BBC Sport. “LIV going out of business, some people will be disappointed and it might not be people that you immediately think of,” Westwood said. He added that “The European tour, I’m not sure it’s such a big win for them.” The financial stakes are high, with the PGA Tour paying £59m last year to keep the alliance alive. The alliance deal was extended in July, but the terms look shaky without the threat of a rival tour. Play Hardball or Walk Away Westwood has a clear message for PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp. If the DP World Tour wants the PGA Tour to keep bankrolling the European side, the price must go up. According to BBC News , Westwood stated he would be “playing hardball and making a lot of demands of the European tour if they expected me to finance it going forward.” The former Ryder Cup hero even suggested that Europe’s best players might be better off playing on the Korn Ferry Tour. This US feeder circuit offers a direct path to the PGA Tour without relying on a struggling European alliance. DP World Tour head Guy Kinnings and Rory McIlroy recently concurred that LIV intended to “destroy” their European rivals. Westwood dismissed this view, noting that most LIV players actually used the European Tour to fill their schedules and earn ranking points. A Robust Defense from Europe The DP World Tour has not acknowledged any weakness, despite Westwood’s warnings. They claim the progress made is remarkable given the havoc caused by the unsustainable model of the breakaway entity. The tour insists that player interest has never been stronger as they look toward the 2027 season. Regarding the new partnership terms, Westwood thinks there are “a lot of questions still to be answered” The PGA Tour holds the money, and the European tour needs a plan that does not rely on free cash from the Americans.

item.title: Ben James Seizes Weekend Lead At World Wide Technology Championship
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Ben James took control of the 2026 World Wide Technology Championship on Friday night in Los Cabos. The rookie’s aggressive 64 (8-under) moved him to 129 (15-under) after 36 holes at El Cardonal at Diamante, a course designed by Tiger Woods. Darkness forced a suspension of play at 5:48 p.m. local time, leaving 12 golfers on the course to finish their rounds on Saturday morning. James now holds a one-shot lead heading into the weekend, according to Sportsnet.ca reporting from the field. During the second round, James made five straight birdies around the turn. He capped the round with a final birdie on the ninth hole. Since turning professional out of Virginia this summer, this performance represents his 14th round of 65 or lower across just 13 tournaments. This victory would secure a spot on the 2028 Championship Series under the new model and move the team into the top 50 in world rankings. Adapting to Professional Pressure James acknowledged the shift in scoring ability required at this level compared to his collegiate days. “It’s weird, in college I was kind of someone that would shoot 2, 3 under every time out and would have trouble going low,” James said. “But you adapt to your surroundings as humans, so I guess out here that’s what you have to do. I’ve been rolling it well and playing well, so nice to be shooting some low numbers.” “I’m doing everything right,” James said. “But for me, I’m just trying to win each shot, just do the best I can for each golf shot and not thinking ahead and just do the best I can. And as I say, winning the shot at hand.” Malnati Chases Contention Peter Malnati sat tied for the lead until a critical error on the par-3 ninth hole. He fell short of the green and missed a 12-foot par putt, concluding his round of 64. The missed opportunity left him one shot behind James. “I work really hard on my game and I haven’t had tons to show for that lately,” Malnati said. “So to not be in that position coming down the stretch on a Friday where … I don’t even have to think about the cut line, I can think about playing golf. That was fun.” Zac Blair shot a 68 to sit three shots behind the leader. Sudarshan Yellamaraju of Mississauga, Ont.James was six shots ahead, He is the top Canadian at 10 under. Ben Silverman of Thornhill, Ont., finished at 9 under, while Adam Svensson of Surrey, B.C., was at 7 under. Nick Taylor of Abbotsford, B.C., also made the cut at 5 under. Defending champion Ben Griffin and fellow North Carolina Tar Heel Ryan Gerard headline the field, with Griffin being one of six past champions competing in Cabo, per Central Oregon Daily . Cut Line and Schedule Saturday morning will see the 36-hole cut announced. Late Friday, 75 golfers were projected to make the cut at 5 under, although two players on the number still needed to finish their second rounds. A recent report relayed by The Peoples Person has named David Raum among the candidates on United’s wish list. The German was also eyed by the English giants this summer, but a move failed to materialise. Meanwhile, Raum’s contract expires at the end of this season and he is yet to sign a new deal, prompting talk of an exit from the Red Bull Arena. item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-ARSENAL-HULL - AFP Arsenal cemented their place at the top of the Premier League table with a gritty 1-0 victory over Hull City at the Emirates Stadium. A 72nd-minute strike from captain Martin Odegaard finally pierced a resilient five-man Hull defence. It was a tactical battle of attrition at the Emirates Stadium as Arsenal eventually wore down a remarkably disciplined Hull City side. The Gunners dominated 67 per cent of the ball and fired off 21 shots, yet they found clear-cut opportunities difficult to come by against the Tigers' low block. A controversial first-half VAR decision to deny Kai Havertz a penalty for offside added to the tension, leaving Mikel Arteta and the home crowd increasingly frustrated as the game remained goalless at the break. The breakthrough finally arrived in the 72nd minute through the persistent Martin Odegaard, who found the space to beat the impressive Konstantinos Tzolakis. While Arsenal's xG of 1.39 suggests they weren't at their creative best, their defensive solidity ensured that Hull’s rare counter-attacks were neutralised effectively. item.title: Brandon Miller’s Groin Injury Threatens Hornets’ $209 Million Future
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images It is that their newest franchise star, Brandon Miller, walked off the court in pain just days after signing the biggest deal in team history. Miller exited Friday night’s game against Boston with right groin soreness, The team suffered a 119-80 defeat, leaving its roster in crisis. A Star In Pain Miller scored eight points early on but started walking gingerly after an alley-oop play in the first quarter. He eventually left the game midway through the second quarter while the Hornets trailed 47-23. Head coach Charles Lee admitted the signs were clear before the substitution. “To be honest, I saw him start to limp a couple of plays. He was good, then he asked for a sub. We’ll evaluate him over the weekend, and we’ll have more information on Monday,” Lee said. Miller has been the bright spot in a dark season. The young forward is putting up career highs of 22 points and 5.3 rebounds per game. Yet he is also in a deep shooting slump, hitting just 36% of his field goals and 26.7% from three-point range according to Yahoo Sports . The team signed him to a five-year, $209 million contract extension last month, the largest in franchise history, because they view him as the core piece to build around after trading LaMelo Ball. A Roster Riddled With Injuries The Hornets were already without Kon Knueppel for Friday’s clash due to a hamstring problem. After missing the first eight games of the season, Knueppel left the ninth due to leg soreness and sat out this contest as well. With Miller and Knueppel out, the team is down to Royce O’Neale, Tidjane Salaun, and rookie Hannes Steinbach as their only forwards. Offensive struggles were rampant. The Hornets shot just 22% from three-point range, converting only 11 of their 50 attempts. In stark contrast, Boston finished with 24 made three-pointers on 55% shooting from deep. Jayson Tatum led the way for Boston with a game-high 34 points in 29 minutes. Naz Reid, Tidjane Salaun, and Sion James were the only Hornets players to score in double figures. The Road Ahead Looks Hard The team’s record has slipped to 3-6 after this sixth consecutive loss. They trailed by as much as 46 points during the game. He now faces another evaluation for a groin issue that could sideline him, the player the team has built its future around. Lee said he will give a more detailed update on Miller’s condition on Monday. Until then, the Hornets must survive without their top scorer and another key forward.

item.title: Joe Milton’s Secret Start: The Eagles’ Plan To Hide Him
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Coach Nick Sirianni admitted he wanted to withhold the news about the quarterback switch for as long as possible. The plan was to spring Milton on the New York Giants instead of Tanner McKee. Sirianni explained his reasoning during a Friday press conference. He noted that every second spent hiding the move gives the opponent less time to prepare. “I was going to hold onto that for as long as I possibly could,” Sirianni said. He emphasized that his main job is to win games and protect the players on the roster. This approach fits a pattern where the coach has used information to create a competitive edge in the past. Milton’s Path to the Field Milton joined the Eagles last month from the Dallas Cowboys practice squad. His career numbers are thin, with only 53 passes thrown and 37 completed. He has two touchdown passes and two interceptions in his professional time. Despite this limited experience, Milton insists he is ready for the pressure. “That’s the thing. We all know that you have to be ready to be on the field at all times. So, I’m going to be ready on Sunday,” Milton said. He added that the coaching staff has done a great job explaining the system to him. He adapted early in life because he was the eldest of seven siblings. Milton sees Sunday as his first NFL start. Teammates Step Up to Help Rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon knows the situation is tough for the new starter. The Eagles have used Lemon in eight games this season. He has caught 31 of his 45 targets for 251 yards and one score. Lemon says the group of wideouts will focus on knowing their assignments and not second-guessing themselves. “Just knowing assignment, execute. … Just practicing, really, just getting extra reps with him, just being more comfortable, just letting him know that you know we got his back, no matter what,” Lemon said. The team is without top receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. Milton will need to rely on his mobility to escape pressure, a skill Tanner McKee lacked during his recent starts. The Eagles hope this change helps them stop a six-game losing streak. The team will take the field on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET against the New York Giants at Lincoln Financial Field.

The Warriors veteran explained that the NBA’s financial rules are generally designed to help smaller-market teams retain their star players. The butt-whooping was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B stage. McCain finished with 21 points on 9-of-14 shooting and five rebounds. He shot 3-of-8 from 3. He also had four steals and one block. Do you think McCain heard Bennett Stirtz's footsteps coming for his playing time? He's certainly played like somebody with a fire lit underneath his seat. Showing an inkling of confidence, the microwave scorer was hot throughout the night. Sure, the outside jumpers fell. But his scoring attack within the paint has also been a nice surprise so far. "Getting those transition shots where you got to guard Ajay, me or Shai, them driving to the basket is awesome for us," McCain said. "They make great decisions. For us, we just continue that. At halftime, we just kept our foot on the pedal." McCain had 12 points in the first quarter. He helped the Thunder get away from this one early. As Shai Gilgeous-Alexander gladly took a backseat after back-to-back 40-point nights, it was he and Ajay Mitchell who delivered OKC's first lethal punch to Memphis. item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The team signed former Boston Red Sox starter Sonny Gray to a three-year, $75 million deal. For years, the Braves have required the winning track record that Gray brings to the table. In 2026, he topped Major League Baseball with 18 wins. With a player capable of pitching deep into games, this signing resolves that issue. Fixing a Broken Rotation For a long time, Atlanta has viewed the rotation as a weak spot. A Proven Winner at 36 The Braves have lacked a durable arm, a profile that Gray fits perfectly. He is one of the six pitchers who have logged 160 or more innings in each of the past four seasons. “Not many pitchers of Gray’s age can command a multi-year deal, but he might just do it after recording a 2.72 ERA for the Red Sox and leading MLB in wins (18),” Laws wrote. Atlanta considers him a safe bet because of his ability to pitch in different environments. item.title: Three keys for Northwestern in the Big Ten title game vs. Maryland
item.description: Coming off a dominant 3-0 victory against Indiana, the field hockey team will face Maryland on Sunday in a rematch of a Top-2 clash on October 22nd. If Northwestern wins, it will be the Big Ten tournament champions for three of the last four years and bolster its chance of a third consecutive national championship. It would also be its sixth consecutive national championship appearance. But with so much pressure on this team to win the Big Ten and then the Natty, the Wildcats can’t get too far ahead of themselves. And though they beat the Terrapins 4-2 in their regular-season matchup, that game was far closer than the score would suggest, with Maryland leading for almost a third of the game. item.title: Marc Marquez has shot at eighth MotoGP title after Qatar sprint win
item.description: Ducati's Spanish rider Marc Marquez won the sprint race ahead of the MotoGP Qatar Grand Prix (Karim JAAFAR) Marc Marquez will have the chance to win his eighth MotoGP title on Sunday after storming to victory in a thrilling sprint race in Qatar. Starting from second on the grid, Ducati's Marquez needed to finish Saturday's sprint with five more points than closest rival Jorge Martin in order to have his first shot at retaining his title, and he did exactly that. Marquez is now 49 points ahead of Martin, who put in a brilliant performance to finish third on his return from a broken right wrist, with two weekends to come in the season following Sunday's Grand Prix. The 33-year-old overtook pole-sitter Marco Bezzecchi on the first lap of a race which had to be restarted after his team-mate Francesco Bagnaia was sent flying off the track by Fermin Aldeguer. That heavy crash left two-time former world champion Bagnaia with fractures in his right foot, injuries that have ruled him out of Sunday's race. "It was a strange sprint race especially with the red flag... I was super concentrated," said Marquez. "When I opened a gap I tried to control the race and yeah, 12 points are very important." Aprilia's Bezzecchi -- who posted a record lap time in qualifying -- is no longer a title contender after also crashing out, this time while trying to overtake Marquez. In the meantime Bezzecchi's team-mate Martin worked his way up from 11th on the grid to be on Marquez's wheel, and a second-placed finish would have been enough to ensure the title race be pushed to the next GP weekend in Portimao. But Martin, clearly in pain due to his wrist, slipped back to third behind Fabio Di Giannantonio on the final lap, giving Marquez his chance to win his eighth world crown -- one more than his great rival Valentino Rossi. However in order to seal the deal on Sunday and draw level for premier class titles with Giacomo Agostini, Marquez needs to win the GP and hope that Martin doesn't score a point. That seems unlikely as Martin only needs to finish 15th or higher to deny his compatriot for at least another fortnight, and his performance on Saturday showed how much he's willing to fight on. "I'm really proud of the work I'm doing," said Martin. "When I was fighting with Marc it was really nice, finally I didn't have the power to keep pushing but to be here on the podium is incredible.
